newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN TAKES OVER MORE FUNDS IN CRACKDOWN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN TAKES OVER MORE FUNDS IN CRACKDOWN.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry put investment fund manager CNIS and the AGB IF2 mutual fund under its administration in separate actions in a crackdown on opaque Czech securities practices, ministry officials said on Tuesday.

They are the third and fourth cases of the ministry taking over control of funds and their managers since early November, amid growing calls from investors' for the ministry to clean up dubious activities of players on the Czech securities markets.

CNIS manages two major funds whose shares are traded on the free market of the Prague Stock Exchange -- Cesky Narodni Investicni Obchodne-Podnikatelsky Fond a.s. , and the Cesky Narodni Investicni Majetkovy Fond a.s. .

"The reason (for the forced administration of CNIS) is a failure to correct errors found during an audit last year," Petr Jenicek, an analyst at the brokerage Komero chosen by the ministry as administator for CNIS, told Reuters.

Jenicek said that the Finance Ministry took the action also becasue of "further errors pointed out by (the fund's) depositary officer, and the unwillingness of the management to hand over documents to new organs of the funds."
CNIS, whose full name is Ceska Narodni Investicni Spolecnost, manages an array of smaller unit trusts and funds with assets in excess of 1.5 billion crowns.
According to the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes, the CNIS had overstated the value of real estate in its portfolios, and was buying non-tradable securities of companies connected to CNIS.

"In the activity of the company violations of the law have been repeatedly revealed. Unfortunately, the (earlier) measures did not lead to an improvement," Jeniceck quoted a ministry memorandum as saying.

Marie Jezkova, the head of the ministry's department of investment fund supervision told Reuters that the move on AGB IF 2 was made to "allow time to investigate circumstances" on the fund's statutory change into a holding company.
She did not elaborate.

Many Czech funds have made similar moves over the past year, transforming into a holding company, which can avoid some regulatory oversight and which have barriers to the size of holdings they may have in individual companies..
An auditor, Marie Kucerova, was named as the ministry's administrator of the AGB IF 2 fund, Jezkova said.
The ministry took similar steps last month against two smaller Czech funds, Mercia and Trend, and ministry officials promised that more action would be taken.
The ministry has been under heavy pressure, because of widespread investors' complaints that it was not doing enough to police the funds and the capital markets.

On Sunday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said that the Finance Ministry's capital markets supervision would be cleaved off and fortified as a separate government office which will eventually become an independent body.
AGB IF 2 is a major shareholder of troubled Czech bank Agrobanka a.s., with a 20 percent stake, and the fund's management was connected to Agrobanka.

In the summer, Agrobanka was placed under "temporary forced adminstration" by the central bank because of liquidity problems in a crisis of confidence connected to the failure of another small bank Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank said the crisis was caused by Kreditni's and Agrobanka's connection to a secretive investment group, Motoinvest.
Agrobanka's central bank-administrator is conducting a search for a new majority shareholder to take over management.
-- Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003
